dish: Oden simmered in a light dashi, served since 1915
n: Asakusa Oden Otafuku (浅草おでん 大多福)
w: Founded in 1915 and one of Tokyo's oldest oden houses — paper lanterns, a kept garden and pots of oden simmering in light dashi; a former Michelin Bib Gourmand.
sts: GO TOKYO oden feature (Dec 2024) + Time Out venue page

dish: Grilled-then-steamed unagi with a sauce unchanged for some 220 years
n: Unagi Komagata Maekawa (駒形 前川)
address: Komagata, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (on the Sumida River near Asakusa Station)
w: An Edo-period eel wholesaler turned restaurant on the Sumida riverbank: unagi grilled and steamed until fluffy, lacquered with a tare the house says has not changed in 220 years.
sts: Time Out venue page + Savor Japan classic-restaurants feature (current)

dish: Tendon — tempura shrimp drenched in a dark sesame-oil sauce over rice
n: Daikokuya Tempura, Asakusa (大黒家天麩羅)
address: Near Sensō-ji (Denbōin-dōri side), Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
w: A stone's throw from Sensō-ji, the best known of Asakusa's old tempura houses (with San Sada and Owariya) — queues form for its dark, sesame-fried tendon.

dish: Hakata tonkotsu ramen ordered by form and eaten in solo 'flavour-concentration' booths
w: The Fukuoka tonkotsu chain famous for customising every element on a paper form and slurping alone in a partitioned booth — the Shibuya branch is open 24 hours and a rite of passage for first-timers.

dish: Single-origin pour-over and espresso at Blue Bottle's first store outside the US
w: Blue Bottle's first café outside the US (2015), set in a converted warehouse — its arrival made Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Tokyo's specialty-coffee neighbourhood.
Tokyo's only natural ravine: a kilometre-long wooded path along the Yazawa River below street level, steps from Todoroki Station, ending at Todoroki Fudōson temple.
A riverside garden on the Edo River banks where some 50,000 irises of around 100 varieties bloom in June.

n: Nihombashi Mitsukoshi Main Store (日本橋三越本店)
w: Japan's first department store, descended from the 1673 Echigoya kimono shop; the 1935 building with its bronze lions and soaring atrium Tennyo (Goddess of Sincerity) statue is a nationally designated Important Cultural Property.
